problems.problem: If $n\in\mathbb{N}$, solve the equation $\cos^n x-\sin^n x=1$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$.

Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}$, $a^2+b^2\neq 0$ and $L=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\mid ax+by=c\}$.
(a) Can you find an example of $(a,b,c)$ such that $L=\emptyset$?
(b) Can you find an example of $(a,b,c)$ such that $L$ has a unique element?
(c) Prove that if $L$ contains two elements, then $L$ has infinitely many.

Show that the set
$$A=\{\pm 1\pm 2\pm 3\pm\cdots\pm 2006\}$$
contains an even number of elements.

Find a polynomial $P(X)$ of degree $n$, with real coefficients, satisfying
$$P(X)\mid P(X^2-2007X+2007).$$

An $n\times n$ matrix contains elements only $+1$ or $-1$, such that on any row, on any column, and on the two diagonals of the matrix the product of elements is $-1$. What are the possible values of $n$ ($n\in\mathbb{N}$)?

Find all the polynomials $P(X)$, $Q(X)$ with real coefficients satisfying the equation
$$P(X)Q'(X)-P'(X)Q(X)=1.$$
($P'(X)$ and $Q'(X)$ are the derivatives of $P(X)$ and $Q(X)$.)
In the sequence $\{\sqrt{2},\sqrt[3]{3},\sqrt[4]{4},\ldots,\sqrt[n]{n},\ldots\}$ detect the maximal element.
In a circular cone of radius $R$ and height $h$ compute the maximal volume of an inscribed cylinder with the same axis as the axis of the cone.

Given three distinct integers $a,b,c$, show that there is no polynomial $P(X)$ with integral coefficients satisfying
$$P(a)=b,\quad P(b)=c,\quad P(c)=a.$$

A $3\times 3$ matrix is filled with all the numbers $\{1,2,\ldots,9\}$. The matrix is nice if on any row and on any column there is an even number of elements from the list $\{2,4,6,8\}$. How many nice matrices can you find?
Compare the numbers $P=2010^{2012}$ and $Q=2012^{2010}$: is $P>Q$ or $P<Q$?

The square $ABCD$ ($AB=BC=CD=DA=a$) has its center at the point $O$. Rotate the square anticlockwise with angle $30^\circ$ about the point $O$ and obtain a new square $DEFG$. Find the area of the region $I$ = the intersection of the two squares and the area of the region $U$ = the union of the two squares.

The natural number $A$ has $4$ divisors and the natural number $B$ has $6$ divisors (for example, the number $18$ has $6$ divisors: $1,2,3,6,9,18$). How many divisors could their product $N=A\cdot B$ have?

On a square board of dimensions $1000\times 1000$ the sides of the unit squares are coloured red, green or black.
(a) Is it possible to colour all these sides and to obtain the same number of red, green and black sides?
(b) Is it possible to colour all these sides such that the boundary of every square contains all three colours?
(Each side of a unit $1\times 1$ square is coloured using only one colour; in part (b) we have to consider all possible squares contained in the board, and in this case a side of a $2\times 2$ square can be coloured in one colour or $2$ colours.)

Find all integers $a$ such that
$$\frac{a^2+4}{2a+1}$$
is also an integer.

Let $x,y,z$ be real numbers such that $x+y+z=6$. Prove that at least one of the numbers
$$xy+yz,\quad yz+zx,\quad zx+xy$$
is not greater than $8$ and all of them are at most $9$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $M_1$ a point inside the segment $AB$. The parallel through $M_1$ to $BC$ intersects $AC$ at $M_2$; the parallel through $M_2$ to $BA$ intersects $BC$ at $M_3$; the parallel through $M_3$ to $AC$ intersects $AB$ at $M_4$; the parallel through $M_4$ to $BC$ intersects $AC$ at $M_5$; and so on. Show that after finitely many steps one obtains a closed broken line and find the position of $M_1$ for which the length of this broken line is maximum (a closed broken line $P_1P_2\ldots P_n$ is a finite union of line segments $P_1P_2,P_2P_3,\ldots,P_{n-1}P_n,P_nP_1$).

A group of $61$ students is divided into three subgroups. Two students play a chess game (only once) if and only if they are in the same subgroup. Find a partition such that the total number of games is a multiple of $61$.
